=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in close-up images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely around the stem at each node)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed, serrate (margins have small, sharp, forward-pointing teeth visible along edges)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (long and narrow, tapering to a pointed tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (sharply pointed tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to a narrow base)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs lengthwise with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced evenly, numerous (secondary veins clearly visible and run parallel to each other, extending to margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface smooth and glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, connecting leaf blade to stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, no wings or grooves)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is uniformly green, with slight darkening at nodes)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate seen)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus visible; not applicable as not Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils present)
F. Notes: Some leaves show small holes and minor margin damage, likely from mechanical or environmental factors. The plant is growing in a shaded, leaf-littered forest environment with a tree trunk nearby. The pink tag suggests it is part of a monitoring or research plot. All images depict the same seedling from multiple angles, confirming the whorled leaf arrangement and consistent morphology.
